stories.headline: Juvenile arrested after teenage girl shot and killed at Aurora apartment complex
stories.summary:
A teenage girl was shot and killed late Saturday night at what appears to be the Santana apartment complex on the 9800 block of East Alabama Drive in west Aurora, according to the Aurora Police Department. Officers responded to reports of a shooting around 10:20 p.m. and found the victim with a gunshot wound. She was transported to an area hospital but did not survive.

Aurora police spokesperson Katie Fisher confirmed that a juvenile suspect was arrested a short time after the shooting. The identities of both the victim and the suspect have not been released. The investigation is ongoing.

The shooting is one of several violent incidents in the Denver metro area over the weekend. Four people were also stabbed in Denver's Globeville neighborhood on Saturday, with one person arrested in connection to that attack.

stories.headline: Two Centennial girls, ages 11 and 14, missing since Wednesday night
stories.summary:
The Colorado Bureau of Investigation has issued alerts for two girls who went missing from the 5300 block of South Truckee Court in Centennial late Wednesday night. Auraelia Garcia, 11, and Paityn Maul, 14, were last seen around 11 p.m. and are believed to be together. Law enforcement has expressed concern for their safety.

Auraelia is described as 5 feet tall and 120 pounds with brown hair and brown eyes, last seen wearing a black hoodie and black pants. Paityn is described as 4 feet 11 inches tall and 120 pounds with brown hair and blue eyes, last seen wearing a black hoodie and black shorts.

Anyone who sees the two girls is asked to contact the Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office at 303-795-4711.

stories.headline: Colorado immigration judge found to have violated federal court orders in at least four bond hearings
stories.summary:
Multiple federal judges in Colorado have released people from immigration detention after finding that immigration judge Bobbie C. Masters failed to follow court directives on bond hearings. In at least four cases decided in July, federal judges determined that Masters did not properly apply the required legal standard — that the government must show by clear and convincing evidence that a detainee is a flight risk or danger to the community.

Judge Regina M. Rodriguez wrote on July 22 that while Masters conducted a bond hearing by the court's deadline, the government did not satisfy its burden of proof. Judge Gordon P. Gallagher wrote earlier in July that Masters' decision denying bond 'neither mentions nor analyzes any of the evidence presented by Petitioner, leaving the distinct impression that nothing Petitioner presented was considered.'

The rulings are part of a broader wave of habeas corpus petitions flooding Colorado's U.S. District Court over the past year, most alleging improper denial of bond hearings to immigration detainees. The Denver-based federal appeals court recently issued a binding interpretation of the law confirming that many detainees are entitled to bond hearings. Masters was appointed as an immigration judge in 2022 and previously practiced immigration law in Denver.

stories.headline: Democrat Jessica Killin outraises incumbent Republican in bid for Colorado's historically red 5th Congressional District
stories.summary:
Democrat Jessica Killin has outraised incumbent Rep. Jeff Crank by $1.3 million in Colorado's 5th Congressional District race, which centers on Colorado Springs and has never been won by a Democrat in any of its redistricted configurations. Killin, an Army veteran and former congressional chief of staff, won her primary and enters the general election with more cash on hand than Crank.

The district has been shifting incrementally toward competitiveness in recent cycles — an underfunded Democratic challenger cracked 40 percent of the vote in each of the last two general elections, and independent Yemi Mobolade upset a Republican in the 2023 Colorado Springs mayoral race. A recent poll released by Killin's campaign shows competitive numbers heading into the fall.

Analysts point to national headwinds — including tariffs, immigration enforcement controversies, and the ongoing U.S. involvement in Iran — as factors that could benefit Killin. The race is among those being watched as Colorado Democrats simultaneously pursue a supermajority in the state legislature.

stories.headline: Denver opens cooling centers as Heat Advisory extends through Monday amid near-100-degree temperatures
stories.summary:
A Heat Advisory is in effect for the I-25 corridor through late Monday evening as afternoon temperatures climb into the upper 90s and lower 100s across the Denver metro area and eastern plains. Denver has opened cooling areas at libraries and recreation centers, though advocates are calling on the city to expand access for families and people experiencing homelessness.

A cold front is expected to move through Colorado on Monday, potentially bringing earlier relief to northern areas while southern locations remain near 100 degrees. A noticeable cooldown to the mid-80s is forecast for Tuesday, with temperatures gradually rebounding toward 90 degrees by Wednesday.

Residents are advised to stay hydrated, take breaks from the heat, and check on vulnerable neighbors. The extreme heat is compounding Colorado's ongoing drought conditions, which have already led to record-low streamflows and fishing closures across the state.

stories.headline: 9/11 World Trade Center steel beam comes to Denver as part of 25th anniversary national tour
stories.summary:
The Tunnel to Towers Foundation brought a 21-foot, 16,900-pound steel beam recovered from the South Tower of the World Trade Center to Denver on Saturday as part of its Steel Across America tour, marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. The beam was displayed at the Wings Over the Rockies Air & Space Museum, which served as the tour's 27th stop on a cross-country journey spanning more than 10,500 miles.

The ceremony featured a color guard presentation, a pipes and drums procession, the national anthem, and remarks from retired FDNY Battalion Commander Jack Oehm and Stephen Siller Jr., whose father, firefighter Stephen Siller, was killed responding to the attacks. Wings Over the Rockies President and CEO David Dickerson received a commemorative steel flag containing original World Trade Center steel.

The tour will next stop at the National WW1 Museum and Memorial in Kansas City, Mo., before concluding at Ground Zero on Sept. 11, 2026.

stories.headline: East Colfax bar owner blames BRT road construction after flooding causes $30,000 in damage
stories.summary:
A Denver bar owner on East Colfax Avenue says heavy rainfall Friday sent approximately three feet of water into his business's basement, causing an estimated $30,000 in damage and forcing a temporary closure. The owner contends that construction tied to Denver's Bus Rapid Transit project on Colfax contributed to the severity of the flooding by altering drainage patterns near his building.

The flooding raises questions about how the ongoing BRT construction — already a source of concern for Colfax Avenue businesses — may be affecting stormwater management along the corridor. The bar owner said the damage threatens the building's future viability.

Denver's East Colfax BRT project received $150 million in federal funding earlier this year, protecting it from service cuts, but the construction timeline has drawn ongoing scrutiny from local business owners who say the disruption is harming their livelihoods.

stories.headline: Denver Water urges conservation as historic drought leaves state Capitol lawn brown and streams near crisis
stories.summary:
Denver Water is ramping up conservation messaging as Colorado's historic drought leaves visible marks across the metro area, including a blotchy, brown lawn at the state Capitol that the utility is holding up as a symbol of responsible water use. Stream temperatures on the West Slope have routinely hit 75 degrees this summer due to extreme low flows, threatening aquatic life and prompting fishing closures.

Kirk Klancke, president of the Colorado Headwaters Chapter of Trout Unlimited and a longtime water monitor, says Denver's reliance on Kentucky Bluegrass — a non-native grass suited for climates with 38 to 58 inches of rain annually — is unsustainable in a city that typically receives about 15 inches per year, and has received only 4 to 7 inches so far in 2026. He estimates that about 60 percent of Denver's water use goes toward landscape irrigation.

Fishing and rafting contribute approximately $2.5 billion to Colorado's economy annually, and 2026 has been a damaging season for both industries due to closed streams and low water levels. Klancke's spring-fed pool in Fraser has dried up for the first time in 28 years, signaling that groundwater supplies are declining alongside surface flows.

stories.headline: Proposed Denver data center estimated to use 805,000 gallons of water per day amid statewide drought
stories.summary:
A proposed new data center in Denver has drawn scrutiny for its projected daily water use of approximately 805,000 gallons — equivalent to what an average household would consume in more than 11 years — at a time when Colorado is experiencing a historic drought and record-low streamflows. Colorado is home to at least 57 data centers, which use water primarily for cooling systems.

Critics argue that the rapid expansion of data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure is placing unsustainable demands on Colorado's already-strained water supplies. Proponents of the industry counter that agricultural water use is far larger in scale.

The controversy highlights a growing tension in the Denver metro area between the economic benefits of tech infrastructure development and the environmental costs of water-intensive facilities during an extended drought emergency.

stories.headline: Colorado Rapids win 1-0 in stoppage time over Austin FC; star defender Lucas Herrington linked to Premier League transfer
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rapids claimed a dramatic 1-0 home victory over Austin FC at Dick's Sporting Goods Park on Saturday, with forward Rafa Navarro converting a penalty kick in the 94th minute after being fouled inside the box. The win extended Colorado's recent habit of late victories at home, mirroring a similar stoppage-time result against San Diego FC roughly 10 days earlier.

Navarro drew the foul after a saved shot from Darren Yapi was parried back to him, and was brought down by Austin FC defender Przemyslaw Placheta. Head coach Matt Wells praised the team's resilience, saying the performance showed fantastic character from his players.

The biggest off-field news of the night involved 18-year-old Rapids defender Lucas Herrington, who played all 90 minutes despite reports linking him to a potential transfer to Hull City in England's Premier League. The reported transfer fee would rank among the highest in MLS history. Coach Wells said the transfer situation was off his radar immediately after the match.

stories.headline: Rockies sweep Royals with 8-1 win; Jake McCarthy hits three-run homer as Colorado considers trade deadline moves
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies completed a three-game series sweep of the Kansas City Royals on Sunday, winning 8-1 behind a strong outing from pitcher Kyle Freeland, who went the distance and struck out eight batters in his first career complete game. Jake McCarthy added a three-run home run to pace the offense.

The sweep comes as the MLB trade deadline approaches Monday at 4 p.m., with McCarthy and pitcher Antonio Senzatela among Rockies players who have drawn trade interest. The Rockies have been in rebuilding mode and a decision on whether to move veterans at the deadline will signal the organization's direction for the remainder of the season.

McCarthy made history earlier in the season by hitting two inside-the-park home runs in 2026, a feat that had not been accomplished by a single player in a single MLB season before this year.

stories.headline: Nuggets to re-sign restricted free agent Spencer Jones; Peyton Watson sign-and-trade talks continue with Hawks
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets are moving to retain restricted free agent Spencer Jones, re-signing the young guard ahead of what could be a significant roster reshaping this offseason. The move signals the team's confidence in Jones as a rotation piece going into the 2026-27 season.

Separately, talks surrounding a potential sign-and-trade of forward Peyton Watson to the Atlanta Hawks are ongoing, with Denver having lowered its asking price in recent days. Watson, a former first-round pick, has drawn interest from Atlanta as both sides work to structure a deal before the free agency period closes.

The Nuggets also face a major contract decision on the horizon, with star center Nikola Jokic eligible for a five-year supermax extension next summer that is estimated to be worth approximately $350 million — which would mark the second time he has signed the richest contract in NBA history.

topStory.headline: U.S.-Iran Talks in Dispute as Trump Claims Negotiations Underway, Tehran Denies Engagement
topStory.summary:
U.S. President Donald Trump announced over the weekend that he called off a planned large-scale military strike against Iran following appeals from regional allies including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, as well as what he described as a request from Iran itself. Trump said Saturday that American and Iranian officials would meet for talks later that day, expressing optimism about reaching a swift agreement on the Strait of Hormuz and what he characterized as a broader deal on the denuclearization of Iran.

Iran's Foreign Ministry flatly contradicted Trump's account, stating that Tehran is not currently in negotiations with the United States and gave no indication that it had asked the president to stand down any planned strikes. Instead, Iranian spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran is engaged in separate bilateral talks with Oman aimed at establishing a temporary, single-corridor safe passage for vessels through the Strait of Hormuz — a route that would serve the interests of both coastal states. Baghaei added that any such arrangement would not automatically lead to a full reopening of the strait.

The Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical shipping lanes for oil and commercial cargo, has been at the center of the stop-start confrontation between Washington and Tehran. Shipping sources reported some vessel movement in the lane near the Omani coast, suggesting limited activity despite the diplomatic standoff. This is not the first instance during the current conflict in which Trump has threatened military action against Iran and subsequently reversed course.

A CNN exclusive added additional context to the tensions, reporting that a U.S. military officer sent an email to troops ahead of Trump's strike threats seeking what was described as new, creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran — a signal, according to the report, of the limited options available to the administration to compel Tehran into a deal on American terms. The contradictory public statements from Washington and Tehran leave the status of any diplomatic engagement deeply uncertain. Whether the Oman-brokered corridor arrangement could serve as a bridge to broader de-escalation between the U.S. and Iran remains an open question, with Iranian officials indicating they see no immediate need to engage directly with the United States.
